A 10-day-old, 40-kg male Chianina calf
progressive dyspnea, lethargy, and recumbency
temperature was 38.5 °C
heart rate, 170 beats/min with regular rhythm
respiratory rate, 60 breaths/min
jugular pulses were present and mucous membranes were cyanotic
a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur
severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle
a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice
a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum
severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects
agitated saline contrast injected via the left jugular vein produced bubbles in the left atrium and ventricle and exiting the right ventricle through both great vessels

concepts.why: The presence of a grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, a markedly hypoplastic left ventricle, and an interatrial defect are consistent with Tetralogy of Fallot.
The severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects, along with the hypoplastic left ventricle, suggest Tricuspid Atresia.
The presence of severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, along with the interatrial defect, is consistent with Pulmonary Atresia.
The grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur, severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle, and hypoplastic left ventricle are consistent with Ebstein's Anomaly.
The presence of a 6 mm muscular interventricular defect in the dorsal septum and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects is consistent with Ventricular Septal Defect.
The presence of a 16 mm interatrial defect in the upper septum and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects is consistent with Atrial Septal Defect.
The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle, along with the hypoplastic left ventricle, is consistent with Double Outlet Right Ventricle.

concepts.preferred_label: Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries
concepts.why: The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle, along with the hypoplastic left ventricle, is consistent with Congenitally Corrected Transposition of the Great Arteries.

concepts.preferred_label: Double Outlet Right Ventricle with Atrial Septal Defect and Ventricular Septal Defect
concepts.why: The presence of two great vessels arising in parallel from the right ventricle and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects explains the uncovered finding of agitated saline contrast injected via the left jugular vein producing bubbles in the left atrium and ventricle and exiting the right ventricle through both great vessels.

rationales.F06: Cyanosis and jugular pulses suggest right-sided heart disease, which is consistent with multiple congenital heart defects.
rationales.F07: A grade IV/VI right apical systolic murmur is indicative of a significant cardiac abnormality, such as those seen in Tetralogy of Fallot or Double Outlet Right Ventricle.
rationales.F08: Severe dilation of the right atrium and right ventricle is a hallmark of conditions like Tetralogy of Fallot, Tricuspid Atresia, and Double Outlet Right Ventricle.
rationales.F09: A markedly hypoplastic left ventricle with a severely reduced mitral valve orifice is characteristic of conditions such as Tricuspid Atresia and Double Outlet Right Ventricle.
rationales.F10: The presence of an interatrial defect and a muscular interventricular defect suggests a complex congenital heart defect, such as Double Outlet Right Ventricle with Atrial Septal Defect and Ventricular Septal Defect.
rationales.F11: Severe tricuspid regurgitation and bidirectional shunting at both septal defects indicate significant dysfunction of the tricuspid valve and septal defects, consistent with conditions like Ebstein's Anomaly and Double Outlet Right Ventricle.
rationales.F12: The presence of bubbles in the left atrium and ventricle and exiting the right ventricle through both great vessels after agitated saline contrast injection suggests a right-to-left shunt, consistent with conditions like Tetralogy of Fallot and Double Outlet Right Ventricle.
